etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: The adjective is derived from Middle English doughty (“brave, bold, valiant”), from Old English dohtiġ, dyhtiġ (“competent, good, strong, valiant”), from Proto-West Germanic *duhtīg.

The English word may be analysed as dought +‎ -y, and is cognate with Scots douchty, douchtie (“bold, valiant”), Dutch duchtig (“severe, strict”), German tüchtig (“capable, competent, efficient; big; hard”), Danish dygtig (“virtuous, proficient”), Swedish duktig (“efficient; good; capable, clever, smart”), Icelandic dygðugur (“virtuous, stable”).
The noun is derived from the adjective.
senses: (literary or archaic) Robust, sturdy; strong and perhaps stout.
(archaic, rare) A person who is bold or brave.
